chapter: Freelance and studio work in New York
title: Casa Loma at the Paramount and standby pay
summary: He wrote for Casa Loma at 75 dollars each and was offered union standby pay instead.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: the Casa Loma they came along and they wanted to pay me off on standby money when they come in and play at the Paramount and they played there quite a bit. They had a Camel show, the 'Camel Caravan' and --
I remember as a kid my mother taking me to see them and I remember Pee Wee Hunt doing 'The Music Goes Round and Round.' That was about 1935 or '6.
Yeah, I remember it like it was yesterday. In fact, I just wrote something about that recently in another article.
The dates in there, the time in there,
That song, of course, was the craze at that time. And they had, I guess, one of the -- they must have recorded it, he was doing it as a feature on the stage show.

I don't really recall. I wasn't working with them. As I say, they wanted to pay me off. I was getting at that time 75 bucks everytime I would make an arrangement for them, and I would go out and rehearse them. I did a lot of things with that band but it was good. I was busy with other things, and so I didn't go around for any arrangements, but they wanted to give me 50 bucks and they were getting it from the -- either the Paramount or the Union or somebody and the union was giving me up. That's the way it
works. You get paid off in standby money. 50 percent goes to the union, 50 percent goes to whoever you want to hire, and they wanted to pay me off.
